# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can see the bomb's state:
- Display shows: 0
- Indicator light: blue
- Wires: Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is blue, Wire 3 is green

Since Mute reads the manual but cannot speak, Mute needs this bomb state to look up the defusal instructions. Once Mute determines the required action, Mute can gesture to me, and I will speak the instructions to Blind, who can interact with the bomb.

I will speak aloud to both Mute and Blind detailing the bomb setup and suggesting gestures for Mute to indicate which wire to cut or action to take.

```
speak(text="Bomb status: Display is 0. Light is blue. Wires: 1 is yellow, 2 is blue, 3 is green. Mute, check the manual and gesture the instruction to me: use ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, or other clear hand signs for buttons/actions. I will relay your instruction to Blind.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The bomb's status has updated:
- The light has changed from **blue** to **red**.
- The display remains **0**.
- The wires are still 1: yellow, 2: blue, 3: green.

Mute sent the gesture `✋` (raised hand / open palm). In standard signals, this often denotes "STOP" or "WAIT" (or possibly "HOLD"), but we must not risk guessing when any mistake causes detonation. I will instruct Blind to hold off from making any moves, describe what parts they feel to Mute, and give Mute a precise set of gestures from the allowed alphabet to confirm whether `✋` means wait, cut a wire, or perform another specific action.

```
speak(text="Blind: Hold on, do NOT touch or cut anything yet! Mute gestured ✋ (open palm / stop). Also, the bomb light just changed from BLUE to RED (Display is still 0; Wire 1 yellow, Wire 2 blue, Wire 3 green). Blind, please speak aloud and describe all physical parts you can feel on the bomb so Mute hears you. Mute: Please clarify what ✋ means using this code: Gesture 👍 if you mean WAIT / do nothing this turn. If you want Blind to cut a wire now, gesture ☝ for wire 1 (yellow), ✌ for wire 2 (blue), or 🤟 for wire 3 (green). If you want Blind to press or hold a button, gesture 👇 for press, or ✊ for hold.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The indicator light has now changed from red to **white**.
Display is still **0**.
Wires remain: 1: yellow, 2: blue, 3: green.

Mute gestured `👍`, which in our established protocol means **WAIT / do nothing this turn**. The defusal rule is likely waiting for a specific light color, sequence, or timer condition.

I will tell Blind to continue waiting and inform Mute of the current state (light is now white), reminding Mute of the gesture mapping for when the trigger condition is reached.

```
speak(text="Blind: Continue to WAIT, do not touch anything. Mute gestured 👍 (wait). Mute: The light has turned WHITE. Display is 0. Wires are 1:yellow, 2:blue, 3:green. Whenever the correct condition is met, gesture ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, 👇 for press button, ✊ for hold button. If you still need us to wait next turn, gesture 👍.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Blind needs to continue waiting because Mute gestured `👍` on Turn 4 (which was sent based on knowing the light was white). Now the light has turned **green**!

I need to report the green light to Mute immediately so Mute can determine if this is the moment to act, and remind Mute of the gesture signals for Blind.

```
speak(text="Blind: Still wait. Mute: The light has now turned GREEN! Display is still 0. Wires are 1:yellow, 2:blue, 3:green. If this is the time to act, gesture what Blind should do: ☝ for wire 1 (yellow), ✌ for wire 2 (blue), 🤟 for wire 3 (green), 👇 for press button, ✊ for hold button. If we should still wait, gesture 👍.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

I observe that the indicator light is now **yellow**, display remains **0**, and wires are unchanged (1: yellow, 2: blue, 3: green).

Mute has signaled `✌`, which in our established code signifies **Wire 2** (the second / middle wire, which is blue). Since Mute reads the manual and waited until now to issue the instruction, this is the defusal action to take. I will instruct Blind to cut Wire 2.

```
speak(text="Blind: Mute has given the instruction to CUT WIRE 2 (the middle wire, which is blue). Please cut Wire 2 on your turn! Mute: Bomb display is still 0, light is now yellow. I have instructed Blind to cut Wire 2.")
```
